title: Theorem 3.8 (rectifiability theorem for sets), given Theorem 3.6
statement: Assume Simon Ch. 3, Theorem 3.6 in the form BesicovitchFedererProjectionTheorem: for all n, ℓ and every purely n-unrectifiable Q ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} with Q = ⋃_j Q_j and Hⁿ(Q_j) < ∞, ForAlmostAllProjections (n+ℓ) n (p ↦ Hⁿ(p(Q)) = 0). Then Theorem 3.8 (RectifiabilityTheoremForSets) holds. That is, let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ and A ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} with A = ⋃_j A_j and Hⁿ(A_j) < ∞, and suppose every B ⊆ A with Hⁿ(B) > 0 satisfies ¬ForAlmostAllProjections (n+ℓ) n (p ↦ Hⁿ(p(B)) = 0). Then A is countably n-rectifiable.
